# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through gestures, and I need to relay my visual information (display, light, wires) to Blind through Mute, since I can't reach Blind directly... wait, let me check - I speak and Blind receives it (Mute and Blind receive speech). So I can talk directly to Blind.

Let me think about what Mute's gestures might mean. Mute can't see the bomb, so these gestures are likely a request for information, or an attempt to establish a protocol. Since I don't have prior context on what these symbols mean yet, I should first report what I see and try to establish communication with both Mute and Blind, and ask Mute to clarify via gesture what they meant (though Mute can't gesture back at me... wait Mute CAN gesture, since gesture uses hands not voice, and Mute cannot speak but can gesture).

Since it's early, I'll state my observations clearly to both Mute and Blind via speech, since both receive my speech. This gives Blind direct info, and gives Mute the info too (though Mute has no reach either, Mute has the manual and needs to know the bomb state to consult it).

I'll also acknowledge Mute's gestures with a gesture back, since Mute can see gestures too? No - Mute can read the manual, cannot see colors/gestures/printed things (that's Blind's restriction - wait no, re-check: Blind cannot see. Mute's restriction is cannot speak or touch. Mute CAN see gestures presumably, since only Blind has the "cannot see" restriction).

So Mute can see my gestures. I'll gesture back an acknowledgment and speak the bomb details to both Mute and Blind.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 🤟]

Mute is gesturing again after receiving my info. Since I can't hear speech and Mute can't speak, gestures are Mute's only way to signal me directly. Mute likely got instructions from the manual and is trying to encode something using gestures - perhaps which wire to cut, using a simple code we haven't established yet.

Since I have no established gesture dictionary, I can't decode this yet. I should try to establish a simple protocol: ask Mute (via gesture, since Mute sees gestures) to confirm understanding, and continue relaying full bomb state to Blind via speech since Blind acts on it directly.

Actually, thinking about this more carefully - Blind needs actionable instructions, and only Mute has the manual. Mute needs my visual info AND needs to relay manual instructions to Blind. But Mute cannot speak, so Mute can only gesture to me (Deaf), not to Blind directly in a way Blind receives (Blind cannot see gestures). So Mute's ONLY way to influence Blind's actions is through me - Mute gestures to me, I see it, then I speak to Blind to relay.

So I need to decode Mute's gestures. Without an established code, gestures are ambiguous. I should propose a simple protocol: use gestures for wire numbers and yes/no, letting Mute confirm.

I'll gesture back asking for clarification and speak to Blind to wait.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Hold off, don't act yet. Waiting on instructions from Mute via gestures. Bomb state unchanged: display 0, light green, wire1 yellow, wire2 green, wire3 red.")
gesture(to="mute", text="", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute keeps gesturing but I have no established meaning for these symbols. I need to build a protocol from scratch. Since I can speak to both Mute and Blind, and Mute can see my gestures but not hear my speech, I should establish a simple numeric/action code using gestures that Mute can interpret, and use speech to give Blind actual instructions once I understand what Mute wants.

Let me try establishing a basic protocol: I'll propose that Mute use finger-count gestures for wire numbers (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) and 👍/👎 for yes/no confirmation. Mute has been sending 👍✊, 👌✌, 🖐☝, then 👍✊🤟, then 🤟 alone. This could be Mute trying to spell something out or point to wire 3.

Since ambiguity is high, I should propose a clear protocol via gesture since that's the only channel Mute receives from me effectively (Mute can't hear speech either... wait, check: Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? Not stated as unable to hear. Actually the room table only restricts Deaf from hearing. Mute's cannot column says "Speak, or touch the bomb" - no hearing restriction. So Mute CAN hear speech!

So I can speak to Mute AND Mute can hear me. That changes things - I can use speech to establish protocol with Mute, and Mute will understand my words even though Mute can't reply with words, only gestures.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures but do not have a fixed code yet. Let's use finger counts for wire numbers: one finger means wire 1, two fingers means wire 2, three fingers means wire 3. Use thumbs up after the number to confirm cut that wire, thumbs down to say do not cut. Repeat your instruction now using this code.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

Mute responded with 🤟👍 - using my proposed protocol, 🤟 (three fingers) likely means wire 3, and 👍 means confirm/cut it. This matches my established code: wire 3, cut = yes.

I should confirm back to Mute that I understood, then relay this instruction to Blind to cut wire 3 (which is red).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: wire 3, cut confirmed. Relaying to Blind now.")
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the red wire. Do not touch wires 1 or 2.")
```
